rows.document_title: Instrumentation: Cryostat-100 Thermal Insulation Test Apparatus (NASA KSC-TOPS-79, NP-2015-02-1352-HQ)
rows.quote: It is a liquid nitrogen boiloff calorimeter with upper and lower guard chambers and full vacuum pressure range capability.
rows.reasoning: NASA's own description defines Cryostat-100 as an LN2 boiloff calorimeter for insulation k-value measurement (boiloff flow proportional to heat transfer through the test article). The 2015 CTL sheet likewise states the measurement principle is steady-state boiloff calorimetry and lists residual gases as nitrogen, helium, argon or CO2; neither source describes hydrogen dosing, manifold volumes or adsorption-isotherm measurement. It is a different kind of instrument from a volumetric (Sieverts) hydrogen sorption analyzer.

rows.document_title: Instrumentation: Cryostat-100 Thermal Insulation Test Apparatus (NASA KSC-TOPS-79, NP-2015-02-1352-HQ)
rows.quote: The cold mass of Cryostat-100 is 1m long, with a diameter of 168 mm. The test articles can therefore be of a corresponding length and diameter, with a nominal thickness of 25.4 mm.
rows.value_as_printed: test articles sized to the 1 m x 168 mm cold mass, 0-50 mm thick
rows.reasoning: Liquid nitrogen is present, but only inside the cold-mass test/guard chambers as the energy meter. The test article is an insulation layer wrapped on the outside of the cold mass inside the vacuum cylinder, tested at cold vacuum pressures from 760 torr to high vacuum with a nitrogen/He/Ar/CO2 residual gas (same page). The sample is therefore never immersed in a flooded LN2 bath, which is what this key requires (e.g. a hydrogen sorption sample cell dipped in LN2). Recorded as documented absence of a flooded LN2 sample bath, not absence of LN2 in the instrument.
